steps.text: Today we're going to talk about basic mill safety and operation. When working on the machine, I always want to use proper PPE. So this usually is steel tote boots, safety glasses and earplugs. On my milling machine, I have my cutter rotating while my workpiece moves into the cutter. I have three axes. I have my X or side to side. I have my Y or towards and away, and I have my Z which moves up and down. I also have a quill like a drill press to go up and down in my depth as well. If I ever need to shut the mill down quickly, I have a brake on the side here. So if I have this spinning and I ever need to stop it, I shut it off here and pull the brake to shut off the spindle. These cutting tools can spin at thousands of rpm, so I want to ensure that I'm never touching or near the cutter. I want to keep my hands any hoody sleeves, any long sleeves away from the rotating equipment. So to operate my mill, there's a couple things I need to keep in mind.

The first is I have a power on and off switch here. So if I turn it to the one, it spins in one direction. If I spin it to the two, it spins in another direction. I also have my RPMs right here. So if your mill has a variable speed, which most of them do, I need to have my spindle rotating while I change the speed. If I crank on this while it's off, I stretch out the belt and my pulleys lose their position and I will lose the accuracy of my RPM.
On the side, I also have a high and a low gear.
